column2: Radio and newsreels turn engineers, doctors and teachers into symbols of the post-war state. Competence must become more prestigious than battlefield bravado.
'Victory Means a Normal Life'
The campaign's central message is simple: victory is measured not by the number of parades, but by whether people can once again plan their work, family and lives beyond the coming week.
Preparation is still under way, and we support the Party
The Party is still at war with the resistance; the government has not capitulated

An Agreement with District Chiefs

For 50 political power, we will conclude an agreement with the district chiefs. New Monaya and Kreyden will each receive 15 Party influence without destroying underground networks. Separate paid agreements with commanders will become available to prepare additional brigades. Emergency purges will become unavailable: districts must instead be held through influence and interception of announced operations.
The treasury will receive §G3600§! monetary units.
The Presidium's Reserve

We will place an emergency loan through the ministries. The treasury will receive 3600, but raising the funds will cost 50 political power and reduce stability by 3%. The money enters the shared budget before the split; it can be spent on preparation, but is not reserved exclusively for the Party.
Capital Arsenal Orders

Military factories need orders, and the guard needs serviceable equipment. We will organise production of small arms, heavy squad weapons and equipment for headquarters services. Before the split, these are shared state stockpiles: the outcome of the political struggle will determine their distribution.
Garrison Supply Directorate

After choosing Congress defence or a mobile reserve, we will establish a common supply directorate. It reduces supply consumption and accelerates organisation recovery; headquarters remains with the Party when the split occurs.
District Chancelleries

Regional institutions must know which orders are in force and who is authorised to sign them. We will update the registers of Niansas and Hoskheit while maintaining continuity of local administration. This will strengthen the Party's position, but cannot replace work with the garrisons.
The Succession Procedure

Until the very last day, Ivanov's signature held departments together better than any regulation. Now the presidium needs a procedure that will not stop at the door to the president's ward. We will formalise the secretariat's authority and determine in advance who makes decisions when contact with the capital is lost.
Military Transport Columns

The army needs transport in the first weeks of war. Unified headquarters will assign repair routes and coordinate deliveries without waiting for the entire arsenal programme to finish. This focus unlocks a transport order costing 2500 treasury units and taking 28 days; funding and execution remain the government's separate responsibility.
The treasury will receive §G2400§! monetary units.
Restore Administration behind the Lines

We will appoint officials responsible for rations, payments and frontline requisitions. The rear answers to the functioning government: the Congress or a provisional presidium with restored district communications. We will release a reserve of 2400 treasury units and strengthen civilian administration even if the capital has not yet been retaken.
Operations Directorate

Rear administration and reserve management must serve the same operation. Once government communications are restored, we will establish a directorate to coordinate unit requests, replacements and staff plans. Its creation strengthens organisation and planning, but does not cancel the remaining stages of reorganisation.
Charters for District Organisations

Districts will retain some authority over personnel and receive a clearly defined share of responsibility for reconstruction. In return, local organisations undertake to implement the common budget and refrain from creating their own armed formations. These concessions reduce the secretariat's freedom, but make local administration more predictable.
Retain Local Personnel

The war left too few engineers and managers to judge everyone solely by whose orders they followed. District organisations will vouch for specialists. The centre will maintain common standards, but abandon the attempt to approve every appointment personally.
Presidium Personnel Commissions

Emergency appointments must become a permanent system of admission to state service. Commissions will vet managers and build a replacement reserve. This will give the centre more direct control, but taking specialists away from their work will slow reconstruction.
A Single Chain of Command

Hedersett has no intention of governing through endless agreements with every district secretary. Appointments, garrisons and ministerial orders will fall under one system. Strengthening command will require continuing expenditure on enforcement checks.
Restore Revenue Collection

Before choosing between civilian reconstruction and defence orders, the state needs a common financial framework. We will restore tax registers, reconcile port fees with actual turnover and establish uniform payment procedures. Both economic models will rely on regular receipts rather than one-off seizures.
Long-term Port Contracts

A civilian priority must bring turnover to the treasury and a planning horizon to enterprises. We will establish terms for warehouse leases, cargo handling and raw-material supplies. The state will relinquish some immediate control in exchange for lasting contracts.
State Industrial Orders

A military priority requires coordinated production runs, not isolated shipments. The industrial directorate will consolidate orders from the army and related enterprises. Arms output will rise, but contract oversight will remain an expense in the budget.
Council for Applied Research

Laboratories experienced the war differently. Some continued working with the army; others lost personnel and equipment. We will bring the surviving teams into a permanent council for industrial problems, communications and new technologies.
Reopen the Institutes

Once the ministries can again pay their staff and manage state orders, permanent research programmes can return to the institutes. Lecture halls and laboratories must train the next generation of specialists, not merely service departments' urgent requests.

§YKey suspicion thresholds§!
§Y50%§!: the Party can run §Rtwo district commissions simultaneously§!.
§Y70%§!: surveillance enters its crisis stage; new risky operations become particularly dangerous.
§R90%§!: Shabrat is placed on operational watchlists. Suspicion can still be reduced before it reaches 100%.
§R100%§!: if Shabrat is still available, he is §Rarrested immediately§!; lowering the scale does not undo an arrest that has already occurred.

When a commission is active, first prepare a §Yfalse trail§!: it takes 7 days and applies only to the current inspection.

§YThe presidium's task§!
Keep districts obedient, prepare garrisons and consolidate the election result. Apparatus loyalty is not security-service suspicion: 100% loyalty does not mean Shabrat is automatically arrested.

§YUnderground tempo§!
Below §R25%§!, a new operation takes §Y21 days§!; from §Y25%§! to §Y69%§!, §Y28 days§!; from §G70%§!, §Y38 days§!. The first announcement grants another §Y32 days§! to prepare a response. Changes in loyalty do not recalculate a timer already running.

§YOur tools§!
The Security Board unlocks a §Y10-day courier interception§!. A command inspection takes §Y21 days§! and destroys identified local networks, but an empty inspection strengthens Shabrat's position. An agreement with a commander prepares a Party garrison separately. Check the cost and free slot in the decision.

Form an Assault Column

Immediately form one reinforced division using a fixed wartime template. All personnel and equipment are drawn from our actual reserves. Another order becomes available after §Y21 days§!, only while the civil war against the resistance continues. Once it ends, the old prices no longer apply. The Party's reinforced division template retains its original composition until the civil war ends; ordinary recruitment using it is not prohibited.
